regime_note: Per the SPY rows, the broad market is essentially flat over both the last 30 days (-0.29%) and the last 5 days (-0.13%), sitting near the top of its 90-day range — roughly 1% below the 90-day high (757.62) and about 7% above the 90-day low (699.86).

picks.thesis: Convergence: four House members (Fields, Cisneros, Letlow, Allen) bought TSM across Jan-May 2026 in $1-15k bands, alongside an unusually broad same-day open-market insider cluster on 2026-06-05 — eleven TSMC officers including Chairman/CEO Wei Che-Chia, plus VP Yuan's larger $79k buy on 2026-06-22. All insider buys are non-10b5-1. Caveats keep this to medium: the congressional leg is stale and small-band, and individual officer buys are tiny ($3-5k), so dollar conviction is modest despite the breadth. Price sits near the 90-day low (409.74 vs 362.50 low, 477.57 high), down ~7% over 30 days.
key_risks: Individual insider dollar amounts are very small, so breadth overstates conviction
Foreign-officer buys may be routine or compensation-linked rather than opportunistic
picks.invalidation: TSMC insiders turn to open-market selling, or the cluster's congressional members file TSM sales.

picks.thesis: Convergence on one name: Rep. David J. Taylor bought IBP four times between 2026-01-29 and 06-15 ($1-15k each), while four insiders made non-10b5-1 open-market buys — COO Wheeler (~$150k) and Director Hilsheimer (~$98k) and CAO Niswonger (~$98k) on 2026-05-11, and CFO Miller (~$13k) on 2026-06-11. Insider dollars are meaningful and fresh (filing lags 1-16 days). Limits: only one congressional filer, and the engine's committee tag rests on Taylor's Agriculture/Transportation seats, a weak fit for a building-products issuer, so discount committee alignment. Price is up ~13% over 30 days.
key_risks: Committee-alignment tag is a poor sector fit and should carry little weight
Buying into an already-extended move (+13% over 30d)
picks.invalidation: IBP insiders file open-market sales, or Taylor unwinds his position while the price rolls over.

picks.thesis: Two insiders bought open-market and non-10b5-1 — Director Aguzin (~$836k, 2026-05-22) and CAO Melamud (~$200k, 2026-06-11) — alongside Rep. Cisneros accumulating across three buys from Jan to June 2026. A sizeable director purchase converging with repeated congressional buying is a genuine signal. The single congressional filer is the main limit. Price sits near the 90-day high (1857.42 vs 1873.88), up ~13% over 30 days — this is buying into strength, not weakness.
key_risks: Name trades near its 90-day high, so the entry is extended
Insider buys, though sizeable, are only two people
picks.invalidation: MELI insiders shift to selling, or Cisneros stops adding while price breaks back down through the middle of its 90-day range.

picks.thesis: Fresh three-member congressional cluster: Reps. Cisneros, Meuser ($15-50k) and McGuire each bought SpaceX between 2026-06-15 and 06-18 (filing lags 14-23 days). No insider data is available (private issuer). Price is marked at 131.11 — the 90-day low — and down ~32% over 30 days, so members bought into a sharp decline. Three buyers falls short of the four-member fresh-cluster bar for high conviction, hence medium.
key_risks: Private issuer with no insider corroboration and opaque pricing
Price already at its 90-day low amid a steep decline
picks.invalidation: The cluster's members file SPCX sales, or the marked price keeps falling below the current 90-day low with no new buying.

picks.thesis: Three-member congressional cluster in AT&T: Sen. Peters, Rep. Tim Moore ($50-100k, filed next day) and Rep. David J. Taylor bought between 2026-06-04 and 06-29, all fresh. Moore's $50-100k band is the largest single ticket among the cluster picks. Price is up ~6% over 5 days and down ~4% over 30 days, mid-range within its 90-day band (21.98; 20.21 low / 26.26 high). Three buyers, so medium rather than high.
key_risks: Largest ticket is still a mid-size band, not outsized conviction
picks.invalidation: The cluster's members file AT&T sales, or the recent 5-day bounce reverses back toward the 90-day low.

picks.thesis: Two senators bought Micron in $1-15k bands — Whitehouse (2026-06-25) and Fetterman, who sits on Commerce (2026-03-30). Two independent congressional signals in semis clears the two-signal floor for medium, but there is no insider corroboration and only these two trades are evidenced. Price is down ~22% over 30 days, well below the 90-day high (853.20 vs 1213.37). Committee proximity cuts both ways — oversight nearness is also why such trades draw scrutiny.
key_risks: Only two evidenced trades, both small bands
picks.invalidation: No further congressional buying appears while price keeps falling toward the 90-day low, or these members file MU sales.

picks.invalidation: The CEO or other insiders file sales, or price breaks below the 90-day low with no follow-on buying.

picks.thesis: Persistent single-filer accumulation: Rep. April McClain Delaney bought Hubbell eleven times between 2026-05-13 and 06-17 (mostly $1-15k, one $15-50k), and sits on House Science, Space & Technology (the engine's semis/tech alignment). Notable for repetition, but it rests entirely on one member with zero insider corroboration, and committee proximity is exactly what invites scrutiny. Price is roughly flat (-1.6% over 30 days), mid-to-low in its 90-day band (482.04; 459.60 low / 556.18 high). Speculative on the single-filer limit.
key_risks: All buys are small bands despite the count
picks.invalidation: Delaney stops adding or files HUBB sales, or price breaks down through the 90-day low.
